title: Latency & Throughput: BlueAnchor Redwood Evaluation
summary: Initial discovery to validate p95 latency targets for streaming and burst token throughput across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer cares about sub-200ms p95 for short chat completions and predictable token/sec during nightly batch enrichment. Security (KMS, SSO, audit logs) and on-prem option required for roadmap. Agreed next steps: send benchmark plan, share security pack, schedule dedicated pilot kick-off call.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private decision factors

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2028-08-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Leah (Redwood SE), John (BlueAnchor SRE), Maya (BlueAnchor ML), Priya (Product), Ethan (CTO)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on throughput/latency, some performance numbers discussed, security checklist.

00:00:02 Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Samir from Redwood Inference. Quick intros?
00:00:10 John: John here, SRE for BlueAnchor. We run the prediction stack for routing and ETA, high volume.
00:00:15 Maya: Maya, ML lead. We're building a conversational assistant for drivers and ops. Need tight latency.
00:00:24 Priya: Priya product, stakeholder for response quality and SLAs.
00:00:30 Samir: Great. Leah's our systems engineer, she'll go deeper on throughput and streaming patterns. Leah over to you.
00:00:36 Leah: Hi all. Quick agenda: understand your p95 targets, concurrency, streaming behavior, and where you'd land on hosted vs dedicated vs private. Also security needs.
00:00:50 Ethan: To be explicit — we want under 200ms p95 for short chat completions (~20-50 tokens), and under 600ms p95 for longer 200-400 token summaries when streaming. On throughput, we expect 350 concurrent chat sessions during peak with bursts to 1.2k for incident surges lasting tens of seconds. Also background batch enrichment ~500k tokens/hour overnight.
00:01:20 Leah: Okay that's super helpful. Couple clarifying q's: for the 350 concurrent, are those all streaming/long lived SSE connections or short request/response?
00:01:30 John: Mix — roughly 60% streaming sessions (driver voice->transcribe->model stream), 40% standard request/response. Bursts are mostly streaming.
00:01:40 Leah: Got it. So two workloads: low-latency short-turn streaming at high concurrency; and higher token throughput for batch. We'll map those to runtime configs.
00:02:00 Maya: Curious what you mean by runtime configs — like batching and cache?
00:02:05 Leah: Yes. Redwood has automatic prefix/KV cache to reuse earlier tokens, continuous batching controls, and quantization profiles. For streaming low-latency we'd reduce batch windows and favor smaller micro-batching and pin models to dedicated workers. For batch we'd use aggressive batching and quantized models to lower cost.
00:02:30 Samir: Important tradeoff — micro-batching reduces token/sec efficiency but helps p95. We can show numbers from our perf harness.
00:02:40 Priya: Do you have precedent for sub-200ms p95 for short chat? We saw some vendors claim it but not in real world.
00:02:50 Leah: We do for optimized model variants on dedicated pools with short sequence lengths; typical results: 150-220ms p95 for 30 token completions on A100/GB equivalents with micro-batching and KV cache. That's with streaming enabled and 64-bit kv config — or, sorry, 8-bit quantization in the efficient path. Transcription fuzz sometimes: the number names get swapped, but the gist is we can prototype.
00:03:15 John: When you say dedicated pools, does that mean reserved GPUs in Redwood Dedicated? We need isolation and predictable tail.
00:03:23 Samir: Yes — Dedicated lets you reserve capacity and set autoscale policies and burst cap. You'll get isolation so your p95 is predictable. If you need on-prem/private for compliance we do a Private deployment with the same control plane.
00:03:36 Ethan: For private we care about KMS/HSM integration; can we bring our own KMS?
00:03:42 Leah: Yes BYOK patterns supported. We integrate with customer KMS and HSM in private deployments; for hosted we'll use Redwood-managed KMS but can do envelope encryption and dedicated key handles if negotiated. We'll share the security pack.
00:03:55 Priya: Audit logs and SSO?
00:03:58 Samir: SSO via SAML/SCIM, RBAC for route-level permissions, and long retention of audit logs available as an add on.
00:04:10 Maya: Back to performance: how do you benchmark token/sec for streaming? We need consistent token/sec for the driver assistant when voice->text->model. If tokens/sec collapses during bursts, the audio latency compounds.
00:04:25 Leah: Our perf harness does token-by-token streaming measurements. We simulate client-side audio frame conversion and measure from first token to last token emitted, tracking inter-token gap and p95 for the stream. For bursts we test increasing concurrency with replayed traces — this gives tokens/sec per worker and joint latency curves. We'll share the harness link (docs/bench links).
00:04:50 Samir: Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/perf-bench (we'll attach). Also we'll include a spreadsheet with expected tokens/sec vs concurrency for model variants.
00:04:59 John: For model variants — are you using open weights or Redwood curated models? We want ability to pick LLMs per latency/cost tradeoff.
00:05:08 Leah: We host a catalog of verified open models and Redwood-optimized variants. For very low latency you can use distilled-variants or quantized checkpoints. We'll recommend and show a matrix during the pilot. Sometimes the transcription writes KV cache as KV cash, sorry — mental slip.
00:05:25 Priya: Cost question — if we pin capacity for 1.2k bursts, cost will explode. How do fallback and routing work?
00:05:34 Samir: Smart routing — you can set policies: prefer dedicated pool, fallback to cheaper quantized or hosted shared pool if dedicated is saturated, or gracefully degrade by reducing max tokens or switching to a cheaper model. Redwood Optimize helps recommend quantization and cache settings to lower unit cost while preserving quality.
00:05:55 Maya: We care about quality regression. If you fallback to quantized model, how do we detect and rollback?
00:06:01 Leah: We integrate evals and quality monitoring with promptsets. You can define alerting on quality regressions per prompt, and automatic rollback to previous model variant. We'll demo in the console.
00:06:12 Ethan: For concurrency isolation — will noisy neighbors on hosted affect us? We run production-critical routing.
00:06:18 Samir: Hosted has soft isolation via rates; Dedicated is recommended for production-critical workloads needing consistent p95. Private gives full customer control.
00:06:28 John: For the overnight batch of 500k tokens/hr — is that cheaper on hosted?
00:06:32 Leah: Typically batch workloads map well to hosted shared pools with aggressive batching and quantized execution. But if you need data isolation for batch results, Dedicated or Private may be required. We'll model cost in our runbook.
00:06:45 Maya: Can we run a pilot that shows end-to-end streaming p95 at our trace replay? Ideally with same infra region and simulating mobile carriers.
00:06:54 Samir: Yes that's the pilot plan we usually run. Steps: you give us a 30-minute bucket of traces (or set of representative prompts + burst profile). We run against both Dedicated config and Hosted and return p95 token timings and cost delta.
00:07:06 Priya: How long does the pilot take and what are prerequisites?
00:07:10 Leah: Kickoff -> onboarding of test keys -> share prompts/trace -> bench run -> results: typical cadence ~2 weeks. If you want Dedicated hardware reserved, add provisioning lead time (1-2 weeks).
00:07:23 Ethan: Can we run an on-prem/private bench with your agents? We are a regulated logistics provider — some driver PII flows through transcripts.
00:07:30 Samir: Private on-prem works; we'd need a small agent to be deployed into your VPC for low latency ingress and we can run bench within your network. That said increases scoping and security review time.
00:07:42 John: About metrics — we need per-token cost, p95, 95th for inter-token gap, and error breakdown for tokenization mismatches.
00:07:51 Leah: We emit per-token latency histograms, p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost-per-request. We'll give examples from prior customers.
00:08:04 Priya: Any gotchas on quantization for streaming? We've heard quantization can increase variability.
00:08:10 Leah: True; certain graph kernels for attention may change numeric behavior. For streaming, we favor stable quant profiles and strong regression tests. That's part of Redwood Optimize recommendations.
00:08:24 Maya: Any suggestions for client-side tuning?
00:08:27 Leah: Yes — reduce chunk sizes for audio frames, use adaptive backoff for reconnects, and prewarm KV cache by priming with frequent prefixes. Also use keep-alive HTTP/2 or websockets to avoid handshakes on short chat sessions.
00:08:41 John: About prewarming — how do you prewarm with Dedicated?
00:08:45 Samir: You can send low-traffic warmup traffic or reserve a minimum pod count. We offer burst policies to handle the 1.2k spikes for short durations.
00:08:54 Ethan: Are there SLA numbers for p95?
00:08:58 Samir: We publish latency SLOs for Dedicated plans and have SLA-backed uptime. Exact p95 contractual guarantees are part of enterprise contracts.
00:09:06 Maya: Anything about network egress — we need guaranteed egress to our VPC for private deployment.
00:09:10 Leah: Private deploy supports customer-managed networking and VPC peering. We'll document options (V-Gateways, sorry VPC peering) and possible latency overhead.
00:09:20 Priya: Can you show a sample run result?
00:09:23 Leah: I can walk through a nearby case — small e-comm customer had 180ms p95 for 40-token streaming requests on dedicated A100-like infra with micro-batching of 4 and KV hit rate of ~45%. Their tokens/sec in steady state was about 4500 tps per GPU, but burst tests showed fall-off at higher concurrency. We'll include the raw trace.
00:09:47 John: That 45% KV hit rate — how realistic is that for us? Our prompts start with variable route IDs.
00:09:54 Leah: You can often cache system prompt prefixes and common utterances — it's workload dependent. We run a prefix analysis on your corpus to estimate hit rates.
00:10:05 Ethan: If we move forward, what's the minimum commitment for Dedicated?
00:10:09 Samir: Typically a monthly reserved baseline; we'll give a few options in the quote. Pilot can run with reserved trial capacity or hosted runs.
00:10:18 Priya: Anything else we should know about streaming tokenization differences?
00:10:21 Leah: Tokenization variance across model families can alter token counts; we normalize by measuring token throughput rather than raw token count.
00:10:30 Maya: Great. Let's talk about next steps.
00:10:34 Samir: Recap — BlueAnchor to share: 1) representative prompt set and two trace snippets (one peak, one steady), 2) desired p95 target matrix, 3) security constraints (KMS/PII). Redwood to share perf harness link, security pack, and pilot config. Kickoff next week.
00:10:56 John: Sounds good. Priya — I'll follow up with the prompts.
00:11:00 Priya: Yup.
00:11:05 Samir: Anything else?
00:11:07 Ethan: One question — competitors: we are also looking at Anthropic and OpenAI. Any direct comparisons you can provide?
00:11:14 Leah: We have benchmark comparisons in the perf pack but note model family differences — we'll focus on latency/cost curves for your workload rather than generic head-to-heads.
00:11:26 Samir: Ok let's end here. Thanks everyone. We'll send materials.
00:11:30 (call recording stops)

Notes: transcript has a few mis-transcribed bits (KV cash, V-Gateways) which will be cleaned in official notes. Attachments mentioned: https://docs.redwood.ai/perf-bench, security pack link (to be attached), pilot config template in follow up.
